policy.label: Policy P3.2: Renewals and follow-up consults
policy.text:
Each prescription covers a set number of monthly repeats. While a patient is on a plan they have a follow-up consult every 3 months, included in the plan price. When the repeats are about to run out, they need a renewal consult. We email a reminder 21 days before the last repeat is used. A renewal can be done at a booked follow-up if it falls before the next billing date.

Patients should book a renewal consult at least 7 days before their next billing date. If the new prescription is not approved by the billing date, we hold the plan charge and the order waits in script pending; we charge once the prescription is approved, so nobody pays for an order that cannot be sent. Renewal consults on an active plan cost nothing extra. A patient whose plan was cancelled for less than 6 months can restart on their existing prescription if it still has repeats; otherwise they need a new consult.

Agents can book and explain renewals. Only a clinician decides whether to renew a prescription and what is prescribed.

policy.label: Policy P7.1: Appointments
policy.text:
Consults are by phone or video with one of our clinicians, Monday to Friday 8 am to 8 pm and Saturday 9 am to 1 pm, local time. Patients book, move or cancel in their account, or support can do it for them. A booking can switch between phone and video at any time before the consult.

Moving or cancelling is free up to 24 hours before the consult. Within 24 hours, one free reschedule is allowed. The clinician calls at the booked time, and tries twice over 10 minutes before marking the consult missed.

Missed consults. The first missed consult in 6 months has no fee; we rebook it. A second missed consult within 6 months carries a missed-consult fee of A$45, NZ$49 or £30. A carer or family member can join a consult with the patient's consent.

policy.label: Policy P3.1: Prescriptions, dispensing and dispatch
policy.text:
Order statuses. Script pending: a clinician is approving a new prescription and sending it to our partner pharmacy. This usually takes up to 2 business days after the consult. Dispensing: the pharmacist checks and packs the order, usually within 1 business day. Shipped: the order is with Courierline and has a tracking number. Delivered: Courierline has recorded the delivery.

Repeat orders on an existing prescription skip script pending. They are placed on the billing date and go straight to dispensing. Orders dispensed by 2 pm local time are dispatched the same business day; otherwise the next business day. Orders placed on a weekend are processed on the next business day. So a repeat order is usually dispatched 1 to 2 business days after the billing date.

Agents cannot speed up a prescription approval or add products to an order. They can check the status, explain it, and pass a request to a clinician.
